dedupe_keys.name: west africa coastal vulnerability mapping commercial crop production 2000 nasa sedac ciesin

description: Five-arc-minute rasters of crop production, in metric tonnes per grid cell, for five higher-value export crops in coastal West Africa: cocoa, bananas, coconut, palm oil and rubber. The NASA Earthdata catalogue page says the layers belong to the West Africa Coastal Vulnerability Mapping series, because some of these commercial crops are at high risk from sea level rise and storm surge, and that production was derived from the harvested area and yield rasters of the M3-Crops collection (Monfreda et al., 2008), which covers 175 crops. Version 1.00 was released by CIESIN through SEDAC in 2018; the bounding box runs from about 1.65 to 13.9 degrees north and 16.7 degrees west to 16.2 degrees east. Data are openly shared under the EOSDIS data use and citation guidance, free to download after an Earthdata login, with a README. Caveats: values represent about 2000, and they inherit M3-Crops' downscaling of national statistics. For simulation it gives the exposure of export crop production along the West African coast to coastal flooding and sea level rise, which can be joined to port and export chain models. Related catalogue records include EarthStat global agricultural geodata and FAO-IIASA GAEZ.
